title: The Wobbly Tower Trick
markdown:
It was a sunny day in Whispering Woods, and tummies rumbled for ruby-red berries. The berries hung high. Too high.

“We need a tower!” chirped Noah, the little bluebird.

“A cushion tower!” rumbled Buttons, the fluffy bear cub.

Ranger Tess stood by with a picnic cloth and did not gather anyone around. She watched them try.

First try: a bouncy tumble. Noah sat on a cushion. Buttons added another on top, then another that was bigger than the one below. Wibble-wobble. Down they went in a heap of giggles, Noah’s feathers sticking out at funny angles, Buttons’ fur full of grass.

“Again,” Tess said. “Biggest, softest cushion at the very bottom.”

Buttons nudged the giant cushion into place. A wide, soft base that did not mind being sat on. Then a medium cushion, then a smaller one, like steps made of cloud. Noah hopped on top, one careful claw at a time.

He stood tall and steady. No wobbles. The berries were suddenly a beak away.

“Hooray!” Noah chirped.

“It didn’t wobble!” Buttons clapped, which made the tower shiver once and then remember its job.

Tess pointed at the wide bottom, not at a secret of the universe. “Heaviest bits low down. Everything balanced. Steady.”

They looked at the tower, then the berries. Perfect. They munched, juice on beaks and paws, the tower still standing because nobody had put the giant cushion on top this time.

“So heavy things on the bottom make it stand up straight?” asked Buttons.

“Exactly. A useful way to build.”

Noah swallowed a berry and did not wonder what other wobbly things they could steady. He hopped down the small cushion, the medium, the giant, and left the stack ready for the next hungry afternoon. Buttons sat on the picnic cloth and guarded the leftover fruit, which was, in its way, another kind of base.
